newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Loss-making Gulf Air to cut more jobs.
newsitem.headline: Loss-making Gulf Air to cut more jobs.

text.p: Loss-making regional carrier Gulf Air plans to axe at least 400 more jobs this year to cut costs, Bahrain's Gulf Daily News said on Monday.
"At least 400 more jobs are to be axed under Gulf Air's cost-cutting campaign," the newspaper, quoting unnamed sources, said.
Officials of Gulf Air, owned by the governments of Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi emirate in the United Arab Emirates, were not immediately available for comment.
The newspaper said the airline's current staff strength was about 5,300 after scores of employees were sacked or offered early retirement.
"The company plans to further reduce its staff strength to between 4,700 and 4,900 by the end of this year," it said.
Areas being looked at for further cuts are the computer, medical and transport departments, all of which are manned mainly by Bahrainis, it added.
In February, Gulf Air sacked 40 staff -- 15 Bahrainis, 24 Omanis and a Qatari. Another 100 employees were told to take early retirement.
The Bahrain-based airline posted $67 million operating losses in 1996 after suffering a net loss of $159 million in 1995.
Gulf Air president and chief executive Sheikh Ahmed bin Saif al-Nahayan said last week the owners would grant the airline a $200 million loan.
